objective: T-20260929-11: does an elastic net trained on 8 quarters of SUE (eps and revenue) history, expanding-window yearly refit, add out-of-sample net-of-cost value over single-quarter SUE and 12-1 momentum on the S&P 500 pool, and clear the runbook section 5 keep tiers?

sources.core_claim: Elastic net models that use several quarters of standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) history forecast returns better than one-quarter SUE or streak features: models with up to 12 quarters beat shorter-horizon and streak-based approaches in returns, Sharpe ratio and alpha; Sharpe ratios nearly double, alphas stay significant after controlling for one-quarter SUE and streak effects; gains are strongest among large caps, where the latest surprise is priced quickly but older surprises are overlooked.
sources.project_applicability: Defines the tested design: multi-quarter SUE history -> elastic net -> long-short/long portfolio; large-cap emphasis motivates the S&P 500 pool.
sources.reflection: Only the abstract could be read: features beyond 'up to 12 quarters of SUE' (revenue surprise? streak count definition?), label horizon, out-of-sample design, costs and reported Sharpe are unknown. Paper's SUE is built from announcement-date data (Compustat/IBES style); ours is visible only at the 10-Q/10-K filing date, which lags the earnings press release, so the announcement-day reaction is missed and PEAD measured here is post-filing drift.

sources.core_claim: Stock prices fully reflect earnings surprises on the announcement date; large-cap PEAD vanished by about 2006 and microcap PEAD disappeared later.
sources.project_applicability: Prior against any PEAD signal in the S&P 500 pool; the multi-quarter idea must beat this by using older, not latest, surprises.
sources.reflection: Abstract only; tests the last-quarter surprise, not multi-quarter history.

sources.core_claim: Earnings momentum (SUE-sorted deciles) earns about 0.9% per month over 1972-1999 in the US; price momentum is largely a manifestation of the systematic component of earnings momentum, though both carry independent information.
sources.project_applicability: Justifies the 12-1 momentum baseline and the ENET_MOM combination candidate.
sources.reflection: Search summary only; small-cap identified; pre-decay sample.

sources.core_claim: A small set of variables tied to momentum, liquidity and limited arbitrage explains PEAD directly and consistently, found with double machine learning over a high-dimensional set.
sources.project_applicability: Supports adding a momentum baseline and warns the SUE-history signal may be a proxy for momentum/liquidity; large-cap S&P pool removes most limits-to-arbitrage variation.
sources.reflection: Explains PEAD, not a trading strategy; abstract only.

sources.core_claim: Combines SUE-style quantitative earnings surprises with LLM-extracted earnings-call language; reports improved out-of-sample prediction over either signal alone; uses EODHD prices and OpenAI models.
sources.project_applicability: Recent (2026) evidence that SUE numbers still carry signal but adds text; text/LLM route is out of this task (no bulk LLM labeling).
sources.reflection: Summary-level read; no Kaczmarek-Zaremba replication in it; different data.

sources.core_claim: Two 2025 papers claim PEAD resurged (Dickerson-Julliard-Mueller, JFE forthcoming; Hirshleifer-Peng-Wang, RFS 2025); Subrahmanyam (2025) using 2001-2024 US data finds the drift t-stat falls from 2.18 to 1.43 (insignificant) after excluding the bottom 20% by market value, i.e. microcaps (3% of market value) drive it.
sources.project_applicability: Large-cap pool has no microcaps; expect little classic PEAD there, so any gain must come from the multi-quarter information.
sources.reflection: Secondary summary of a working paper.

sources.core_claim: TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits, gap) yields expanding training sets and a validation block after each, dropping `gap` samples between train end and validation start to reduce leakage.
sources.project_applicability: Hyperparameter selection uses TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=4, gap=1) on unique training months (one-month gap between label periods).
sources.reflection: Gap counts samples; we apply it to month groups, then map back to rows.

sources.core_claim: Single-quarter XBRL SUE at the first session after filing: CAR +0.71% over 20d (t 3.6; 2024+ +0.82%) but it does not beat the redated placebo; calendar-time book -3.9%/yr full, +1.5% 2024+ at 20bp; SUE rank among recent reporters IC 0.016 (t 1.2).
sources.project_applicability: Direct predecessor; the present task differs by multi-quarter history, a regularised model and an S&P 500 large-cap pool.

sources.core_claim: Moving visible_at to the 8-K announcement time did not recover a tradable effect: t_dates 1.064 < 3, beats_redated False, book_positive_20bp False in both windows.
sources.project_applicability: Shows the filing-date lag is not the sole reason single-quarter SUE fails on our data.

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: Added a single-quarter SUE baseline, a 12-1 momentum baseline and their rank-sum with the model (Chordia-Shivakumar, Hansen-Siggaard), plus a label-shuffle and a random-pick placebo, because the primary paper's full text (label, costs, OOS design) could not be read and the model's incremental value must be shown locally.
